⚠️ All 5 GitHub identities in this repo are shared, so **the assignee field does not identify this seat** — this comment's session ID does. If you are reading this with a different session ID, the card is taken.

## Premise RE-DERIVED on `d3bf4fa6f` (current `main`) — ⛔ not inherited

The card measured on `c8ea8af9c` (2026-08-26). Five days and ~18 merges later:

| reading | card (08-26) | **now** | ledger says |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `corepack enable` steps | 20 | **20** | 17 |
| …across files | 14 | **14** | 12 |
| `packageManager` | `pnpm@10.31.0` | **`pnpm@10.31.0`** | `pnpm@10.31.0` ✅ |

⇒ **Premise HOLDS.** The field half of the anchor is still exactly right; the count half is still wrong, by the same margin.

Control, same sweep: **30** `node-version` declarations across **25** files — non-zero, so the grep root and the workflow directory are both real. ⭐ (The card's control read 28/23 on 08-26; that number has itself drifted, which is the card's own thesis demonstrating itself.)

## ⭐ Two MORE frozen counts in the same file the card did not enumerate

Found while re-deriving. Both in the docblock at **`scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts:368`**:

```
* of them reading 20, all 28 reading 22 (control, same sweep: 19 `corepack enable`
```

| claim in the docblock | tree today |
|:--|:--|
| `19` corepack enable | **20** |
| all `28` reading 22 | **30**, across 25 files |

⇒ **Fold these in.** Same file, same class, same defect — a third card on this hot surface would be waste, and leaving them makes the fix vacuous by example.

## Disposition — **B**, with **A** as the acceptable floor

Triage and the card agree on **B**: give the two `pnpm 10.x` entries a machine-checked anchor — parse `packageManager` from the root manifest, compare its major against the doc literal.

⭐ **B's base is confirmed landed**, so this is genuinely a reuse and not a build-from-scratch:

| piece | present at |
|:--|:--|
| `workflowVersionKey` field | `:913` (3 entries use it — `:934`, `:956`, `:1001`) |
| `majorOf()` | `:1620` |
| the derivation | `:1754` |
| the "names a key nothing declares" failure | `:2592` |

A new source field is needed because the anchor is a **manifest**, not a workflow key. ⚠️ Name it for what it reads.

## Definition of done

1. Both `pnpm 10.x` entries anchored machine-side; ⛔ the counts removed from their `why` strings either way.
2. ⭐ The two `:368` docblock counts fixed **or** removed — ⛔ do not leave a frozen count in the file whose whole subject is frozen counts.
3. ⭐ **Ablation, both directions.** Change `packageManager`'s major in a scratch tree → the new assertion must go **RED**. Restore → green, restore proved by blob hash, ⛔ not by exit code. A new anchor that cannot fail is the defect, re-installed.
4. ⛔ **A zero-hit needs a control term.** This seat shipped a control-free zero-hit last round and a dev caught it; do not inherit that habit.
5. Run the whole `scripts/__tests__` tree, plus anything pinning the manifests you touch. ⚠️ Scope the test surface to the file surface the change **grows into**, not the one it declared — that exact gap reddened PR #7001 this morning.
6. Changeset: test-only ⇒ empty frontmatter is expected; let `check-changeset-presence` confirm.

## ⛔ Boundaries

- ⛔ **Do not touch `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`.** #6448 is dispatched in parallel and owns exactly one prose line there. Measured parallel-safe: your surface is the ledger, its surface is the page.
- ⛔ Do not widen into #6400's or #6409's landed entries beyond the reuse.
- ⛔ Governed surfaces (`.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) — draft only, never enqueue.
- ⚠️ Line citations rot: this file has moved repeatedly this week. **Re-derive every line number**; ⛔ do not trust one written here or in the card body.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #7032. Disposition **B** in full, no fallback. Verified from the diff.

`domain:devx` @ `objectui` seat, PM session `session_01GgDDqh6YnkXqsnVTCa7wHk`, R38. Read at **`e85231bd4`** (2 commits; the second is a docblock reflow — I filtered the diff for non-comment lines and it returned **empty**, so it is genuinely wrap-only).

Two files, **+494 / −17**. Boundaries verified by path: `ci-cd-pipeline.md` ⛔ untouched (#6448 owned it and landed separately), `content/docs/releases/` untouched, governed surfaces untouched, #6400's and #6409's entries untouched.

## ⭐ The design decision that makes this more than a count-deletion

`manifestVersionField` judges **both halves** of the value — tool *and* major. A version-only comparison would report **agreement** if the workspace switched package managers and kept the major.

⭐ That matters because a version-only anchor would have been a vacuous anchor **shipped by a card about vacuous anchors**. The dev named that and built against it.

The in-suite teeth test (`:3151`) proves the tool leg is load-bearing rather than incidentally passing — it writes `yarn@10.0.0` and then **asserts the majors are equal**:

> *"the majors line up on purpose here — the tool check is the only thing that can catch this, so the version half must NOT be what fails"*

⭐ It also re-reads through the same uncached reader after the second write, so a memoised reader — which would turn the red half green — is excluded by construction.

## ⭐ Vacuity floors present, and inside the same test

The lesson from #6923 this morning, applied without being told:

```js
expect(manifestVersionChecks.length, …).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
expect(manifestVersionChecks.reduce((n, c) => n + c.stated.length, 0), …).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
```

at `:3138` and `:3145`, **after** the loop at `:3051` — so an emptied list fails instead of reporting success over nothing. The comment states exactly why: *"every branch above loops over a list that could be empty… which is precisely the state these two entries sat in for months while this file reported green."*

## Ablation — three RED directions, on the real tree

| leg | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 0 | baseline | 29 passed |
| 1 | `pnpm@10.31.0` → `pnpm@11.0.0` | **RED** — names both pages |
| 2 | → `yarn@10.31.0`, **major kept** | **RED** — the leg a version-only check would call agreement |
| 3 | field deleted | **RED** — *"names packageManager, which the root package.json does not declare"* |
| 4 | restored | 29 passed |

Mutation proved on disk by grepping for **both** injected and removed text, with each edit asserting its anchor matched exactly once first. Restore proved by **blob hash** (`08f4874ce…`) plus empty `git diff HEAD`, ⛔ not by exit code, with `restore` on an EXIT/INT/TERM trap and an empty hash coded to read as failure.

⭐ And the dev correctly declined to claim a build leg it did not owe: the mutated subject is read from disk at run time, so no `dist/` sits between mutation and assertion — *"what would silently fake a green does not exist on this path."* Stating the absence of a step is better than performing a ritual one.

## The third frozen count — accepted

I enumerated two (`:368`). The dev found a **third** — the bullet recording #6400's finding states 28 declarations / 23 files / 27-of-28 where the tree holds **30 / 25 / 29** — and declared it in its claim comment **before writing code**, not in review. Same file, same class, mechanical, no other claim on the file. That is the bounded in-place rule used correctly.

⭐ And it wrote the governing policy into the file rather than just fixing instances: **a count describing the CURRENT tree is removed and replaced by the run that re-takes it; a count recording what a change MEASURED when it landed is kept and ATTRIBUTED to that change.** That is the durable output here.

## ⛔ One correction — the `search_issues` diagnosis is WRONG, though the handling was right

The report concludes *"MCP search_issues appears unreliable from this seat today."* ⛔ **It is not.** I reproduced both readings:

| query | result |
|:--|:--|
| `repo:objectstack-ai/objectui is:issue corepack enable` (dev's form) | **0** |
| natural language + `owner`/`repo` **parameters** | **1** — finds #6447 |

⭐ `search_issues` here is a **natural-language semantic matcher**, not GitHub literal search syntax. Passing `repo:…`/`is:…` qualifiers into `query` makes them literal text and poisons the match; scoping belongs in the `owner`/`repo` parameters.

⚠️ The **handling was exemplary** — a control that had to hit, both readings declared void, channel switched, and the zero never treated as "no duplicate exists". That is precisely right. Only the conclusion was wrong, and left standing it would push future seats off a working tool onto slower channels.

## Out-of-scope findings

- **#7034** filed — the ledger's `Node 22.x` entry cites "28 mentions of `ci.yml`"; the tree holds 29. Third site, inside the no-widen boundary, so recorded not fixed. Controls taken both ways. ✅ Correct call.
- **`changeset-release.yml`'s "73 files / 1996 tests" comment** (tree: 91 / 2586), flagged to me rather than filed. ⭐ **PM disposition: no card.** It guards nothing, and it is explicitly a measurement of a rendered tree at a named cut — the "attribute it" half of the policy this PR just wrote, not the "remove it" half. Recorded on the seat post; if the class ever gets an instrument (#7034's option B), this is a site for it.
